newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest -Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest -Feb 17.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet and Brand-name Products
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- Poland's commercial television broadcasters are increasingly addressing the country's teenage "couch potatoes", who represent important future consumers and already influence many household purchasing decisions, says Jan Hildebrandt, president of RTL 7 Poland. (Media Polska, February 1997)

-- The Czech television commercial for Hohes C orange juice, which says one glass of Hohes C 100 percent juice has as much vitamin C as one half kilos of oranges, sparked complaints from viewers. A test done in Prague's Analab showed Hohes C had as much vitamin C as other juice brands and less than that found in one half kilo of oranges. (Mlada Frona Dnes, February 12, 1997)
-- The Czech Marketing Distribution (CMD) organisation is

beginning the Czech Republic's largest sales promotion. It will send direct mail leaflets to 1.5 million households about food products and other products distributed in 5,000 stores operated by members of CMD. (Pravo, February 12, 1997)
MEDIA AND THE INTERNET:
-- Poland's recently founded Supermedia Internet provider will be the country's leading Internet access provider by the end of the year, Supermedia's president Grzegorz Lindenberg said.
(Media Polska, February 1997)
-- Czech SPT Telecom will begin offering Internet access in late March for an estimated monthly charge of about 600 crowns ($21.15). (Hospodarske Noviny, February 13, 1997)
-- The listed Optimus computer maker has bought a Disney Interactive licence for multimedia production and distribution of Disney cartoons, Optimus said. (Media Polska, February 1997)
-- Polish public radio's "third programme" is now available on the Internet, the radio Internet project manager Lukasz Kunka said. (Media Polska, February 1997)

-- Radio City is Prague's most popular FM radio station in Prague, according to a survey by Media Projekt. In the second half of 1996 the station had 84,000 listeners daily, while Radio Kiss had 79,500, Evropa 2 had 72,500 and Zlata Praha had 70,000. (Lidove Noviny, February 13, 1997)

-- About 5.4 million Polish households watch television programmes broadcast by Eutelsat satellites, which gives Eutelsat a 90-percent share of the audience, according to the GFK Polonia polling institute.(Media Polska, February 1997)

-- Poland's Super Express daily has the biggest share of the newspaper market at 19.8 percent, followed by Gazeta Wyborcza with 18.9 percent, Rzeczpospolita with 9.4 percent, Express Wieczorny with 8.7 percent and Przeglad Sportowy with 6.9 percent, according to a survey by SMG/KRC monitoring firm.
(Media Polska, February 1997)

-- The new Czech television network Galaxie was watched by the same number of young people as Prima Television in areas where Galaxie's signal reaches, says a survey by Rapid Dema. (Lidove Noviny, February 10, 1997)

-- Radio Torun, a commercial FM broadcaster in Torun, northern Poland, has joined the Super FM network of local radio-broadcasters formed by the ZPR entertainment group and Grzegorz Lindenberg. Radio Torun also joined the Pakiet 49 "commercials acquisition system", the company said. (Media Polska, February 1997)
-- Krzysztof Ibisz, one of Polish public television's most
popular presenters, is considering moving to Telewizja Wisla commercial TV station controlled by the ITI holding. (Media Polska, February 1997)

-- Poland's Radio S FM broadcaster, based in Poznan, has installed its new U.S.-made OBI 4.8 KW transmitter at the city's highest point. Its programmes can now be heard in a 100-kilometre radius around Poznan. (Media Polska, February 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS AND MARKETS:

-- A price war has broken out in the Czech Republic's car market, with prices being cut by Japan's Nissan, Mitsubishi and Mazda and by South Korea's Kia and Hyundai. The only European car company to cut its prices has been Italy's Fiat. (Reflex, February 13-20, 1997)

-- McDonald's, which has a dominant position in the Czech fast food market, plans to expand its network of restaurants this year and to increase its assortment of food by adding Chicken McNuggets and McCountry sandwiches. (Hospodarske Noviny, February 10, 1997)

-- Microsoft will launch the Czech version of its new product, Office 97, on the Czech market in April. The English version of the software is already available in the Czech Republic. Office 97 is expected to have huge success since Microsoft sold about 60,000 copies of an earlier product, Office 95. (Reflex, February 13-20, 1997)
-- Opel will begin selling two new car models in the Czech
Republic from February 21. The first is the eight-passenger Sintra, which will cost about 1.1 million crowns and the second is the Vectra Caravan at 524,900 crowns. (Pravo, February 10, 1997)
